settings.heading: Build the ritual
settings.text: Week one is just the habit — pair [brand] with a moment you already keep for yourself: morning coffee, the wind-down, the quiet hour.

settings.heading: Settle into consistency
settings.text: Keep the daily rhythm going. There's no switch to feel for — this is baseline territory, the stuff you only notice by its absence later.

settings.heading: Notice the subtle stuff
settings.text: A good week to check in: mood, presence, how loud your brain feels by evening. Real noticing tends to be gradual and subtle, and experiences vary.

settings.heading: Check in with yourself
settings.text: After several weeks, ask the real question: do I feel a little more like me? That's how [brand] earns its place — or doesn't.

settings.title: Timing
settings.text: Take the recommended serving at a time you can stay consistent with. Use the final label directions as the source of truth.

settings.title: Results
settings.text: There's no guaranteed timeline, and we won't invent one. Those who notice a change describe it as gradual — some don't notice much. Experiences vary.

settings.title: Consistency
settings.text: [brand] is a daily ritual, not an on-demand product — tending, not a switch. Follow the final label directions.

settings.heading: What the first month looks like
settings.lead: [brand] is built for consistent daily support, not an on-demand effect. Change like this tends to arrive quietly — a bit more present, a bit more open, a bit more like yourself. There's no switch to flip. What you notice, and when, varies from person to person.
settings.disclaimer: These are rhythm milestones, not guaranteed results. Individual experiences vary.

settings.label: Stress & Mood
settings.biology_text: Desire runs on bandwidth. When your brain reads the day as one long to-do list, your nervous system stays on duty — and everything quieter gets muted. It isn't a lack of love, and nothing is broken: a mind that never clocks out simply has no room left for wanting anything.
settings.helps_text: KSM-66 Ashwagandha — an adaptogenic root with a long history in Ayurvedic practice — is included to support stress resilience and a calmer everyday baseline. With daily consistency, [brand] supports the settled, present feeling that gives the rest of you room to show up.*

settings.label: Desire & Energy
settings.biology_text: For many women, desire is responsive rather than spontaneous — it rarely shows up first. It tends to arrive after closeness begins, when there's no pressure attached. That's a normal desire style, not a flaw. But it needs somewhere to build: energy left at the end of the day, and a mind at ease enough to notice what it wants.
settings.helps_text: Black Maca, a Peruvian root traditionally used to support desire and energy, is paired with Damiana, a botanical leaf with centuries of traditional use around relaxation and openness. Together they are [brand]'s daily support for the part of you that wants to want.*

settings.label: Connection & Presence
settings.biology_text: Presence is physical. When your mind is elsewhere — replaying the day, watching yourself, waiting for your body to catch up — closeness can feel mechanical instead of natural. Feeling connected to someone else starts with feeling at ease in your own body first.
settings.helps_text: [brand] is built as one small daily ritual, not an in-the-moment fix: the full four-ingredient blend, finished with warming Cinnamon Bark, taken consistently over weeks. Quiet, steady support for feeling more like yourself — and more present when it matters.*

settings.heading: The Science Behind [brand] Desire & Mood
settings.disclaimer: *These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.

settings.name: Black Maca
settings.purpose: The want-to-want root: traditionally used to support desire and energy. Experiences vary.
settings.detail: A cruciferous root cultivated high in the Peruvian Andes for over two thousand years and traditionally taken daily for desire, energy, and stamina. Black maca is the rarest of the maca colors — the one tradition prized most — and [brand] uses gelatinized root, gently pre-cooked the traditional way so it suits an every-day ritual.
settings.source_note: Amounts shown once final label values are approved.

settings.name: KSM-66 Ashwagandha
settings.purpose: For the brain that never clocks out: traditionally used to support a calmer everyday baseline. Experiences vary.
settings.detail: Ashwagandha root has anchored Ayurvedic practice for over three thousand years as a daily tonic for stressful seasons. KSM-66 is a root-only, full-spectrum extract and one of the most researched forms of ashwagandha, studied in human trials in areas like stress resilience, calm, and everyday mood. It's the formula's steady base.
settings.source_note: Amounts shown once final label values are approved.

settings.name: Damiana
settings.purpose: A leaf traditionally used to support relaxation and mood — room to relax into wanting. Experiences vary.
settings.detail: A small flowering shrub from Mexico and the American Southwest, damiana leaf has been brewed for centuries as a relaxing cordial — long associated in traditional practice with ease, openness, and romance. It carries the softer side of the formula: the unwind that makes room for wanting.
settings.source_note: Amounts shown once final label values are approved.

settings.name: Cinnamon Bark
settings.purpose: Rounds out the blend with warmth — and a long history in traditional practices.
settings.detail: True cinnamon bark has warmed daily teas and tonics for about as long as recipes have been written down. In [brand] it plays two roles: rounding out the blend with its traditional warmth, and giving the gummy the cozy, treat-not-task finish that makes the ritual easy to keep.
